ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$. Point $E$ is the midpoint of $OA$. Connect $BE$ and extend it to intersect $AD$ at point $F$. Given that the area of $\triangle AEF$ is $3$, what is the area of $\triangle ABE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a parallelogram,\\
it follows that $AD\parallel BC$ and $OA=OC$,\\
therefore $\triangle AFE\sim \triangle CBE$,\\
which implies $\frac{AE}{EC}=\frac{EF}{BE}$,\\
since point E is the midpoint of $OA$,\\
it follows that $AE=\frac{1}{3}EC$,\\
hence, $EF=\frac{1}{3}BE$,\\
given that $S_{\triangle AEF}=3$,\\
thus, $S_{\triangle AEB}=\boxed{9}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a tilted parallelogram ABCD, AD is above and parallel to BC, and AB is parallel to CD. The two diagonals AC and BD intersect at O; point E is on the segment AO, and is marked as the midpoint of OA; from B connect to E and then continue extending, intersecting the upper side AD at F. Then reason: Set A=(0,0), D=(d,0), B=(u,v) according to affine coordinates, then C=(u+d,v). The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of AC, O=((u+d)/2, v/2). E is the midpoint of OA, so E=((u+d)/4, v/4). The line BE can be written as B+t(E-B). Its y-coordinate is v+t(v/4-v)=v(1-3t/4). Let it intersect AD, that is y=0, obtaining t=4/3. At this time the x-coordinate is u+(4/3)((u+d)/4-u)=d/3, so F=(d/3,0). In the direction of the segment, E corresponds to t=1, and F corresponds to t=4/3, therefore EF=(1/3)BE, that is BE:EF=3:1. Triangles ABE and AEF share the base AE, and B, E, F are collinear, so the ratio of their heights to the line AE equals BE:EF=3:1. Therefore the area ratio [ABE]:[AEF]=3:1. It is known that [AEF]=3, so [ABE]=3×3=9.

The line BE can be written as B+t(E-B). Its y-coordinate is v+t(v/4-v)=v(1-3t/4). Let it intersect AD, that is y=0, obtaining t=4/3. At this time the x-coordinate is u+(4/3)((u+d)/4-u)=d/3, so F=(d/3,0).

In the direction of the segment, E corresponds to t=1, and F corresponds to t=4/3, therefore EF=(1/3)BE, that is BE:EF=3:1. Triangles ABE and AEF share the base AE, and B, E, F are collinear, so the ratio of their heights to the line AE equals BE:EF=3:1. Therefore the area ratio [ABE]:[AEF]=3:1. It is known that [AEF]=3, so [ABE]=3×3=9.
